subject: Admin activity extracts — delivery format, retention, and export Qs
body:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Audit Team <audit@greenline.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Admin activity exports — file formats and retention scope

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As we prepare for Greenline's SOC 2 fieldwork, the audit team needs a concise statement of what Redwood logs for admin-level activity and how you deliver it. Can you confirm the following so we can update our evidence checklist?

1) Which admin actions are captured (create/delete/login/privilege-change/role-assignment/keys/console/API) and whether the payload includes actor IP, user-agent, and request-id.
2) Retention windows by default and options for extended retention or on-demand snapshotting.
3) Export formats you provide (CSV, JSONL, compressed tar, signed manifest), support for incremental vs full snapshots, and delivery mechanisms (SFTP, secure GCS/Azure/S3 presigned, Drive link).
4) How you attest integrity (signed manifests, checksums, HMAC) and whether you support PGP/GPG or customer-supplied keys.
5) Turnaround time for a one-off export (48h/5 business days/other) and whether exports include deleted/soft-deleted items or only current state.

If you can attach a sample manifest and example export filenames, that would be perfect.

Best,
Sara
Sara Li
Senior IT Auditor — Greenline Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity exports — file formats and retention scope

Hi all —

Sharing a short technical snapshot to answer Sara's checklist. I kept the wording audit-friendly; Jordan/Marissa feel free to reword for the legal/commercial copy.

1) Event coverage (admin activity):
- We record: sign-in/logins (console and API), sign-out, failed auth attempts, user creation/deletion, role/permission assignments and revocations, API key/secret creation and rotation events, OAuth client management, service account lifecycle, and explicit administrative policy changes.
- For each event we capture: timestamp (UTC, RFC3339), actor id (internal user id + email), actor IP, user-agent (where applicable), request-id/correlation-id, target resource id, action type, and a short free-text message that includes the API endpoint and request path.
- Sensitive payloads (passwords/secret values) are redacted at source and not present in exported evidence.

2) Retention and snapshotting:
- Default retention: 180 days (admin activity index).
- Extended retention: customers can purchase 1/3/7-year retention blocks in Dedicated/Private tiers or request ad-hoc snapshot exports for Hosted as a one-off.
- On-demand snapshots: we support point-in-time export windows for arbitrary start/end UTC times; snapshots include a manifest and can be delivered as full or delta (incremental) exports.

3) Export formats and delivery:
- Formats: CSV (wide table per event), JSONL (one object per line), and gzipped tar bundles containing per-hour JSONL shards.
- Packaging: every bundle includes a manifest (CSV) listing filenames, record counts, UTC start/end, and a SHA256 checksum column.
- Delivery channels: SFTP (push), presigned S3/GCS/Azure links (time-limited), secure Google Drive folder (link + ACL), or vendor-managed transfer (FTPS) upon agreement.
- Incremental vs full: we support both; incremental exports are delta files keyed by event timestamp and request-id.

4) Integrity and signing:
- We provide SHA256 checksums for every file in the manifest and a manifest-level SHA256 hash.
- For higher assurance we offer manifest signing (HMAC-SHA256) using a Redwood-managed key.
- Customer-supplied signing: for Private deployments we can accommodate customer-supplied GPG/PGP public keys for signing manifests. For Hosted, PGP signing is available under an enterprise contract and a short onboarding step.

5) Turnaround and scope of data in exports:
- Standard one-off export SLA: 3 business days for a standard scoped export (up to 30 days of data).
- Expedited: 24–48 hours available for an additional fee depending on size and retention tier.
- Deleted items: exports include soft-deleted records if requested (we tag them with deletion_ts); permanently purged records are not recoverable once beyond retention/expiry.

Attachments included (examples): admin_activity_manifest_sample.csv (manifest layout), checksums.sha256 (sample checksum file), small JSONL export shard.

Let me know if you want sample filenames and a stub example (I can attach them).

-Ben

Adding the operational/commercial side:
- Cost: one-off standard exports (<= 30 days, <100GB) are included for enterprise customers as part of the SOC2 evidence window; larger or recurring extended retention exports fall under an evidence handling fee schedule — we can share the rate card on request.
- Access: for Hosted customers we surface temporary read-only Drive links (ACLed to a Greenline audit alias) and presigned S3 for direct ingest into auditor tooling.
- Custody & audit trail: we provide an attested manifest and chain-of-custody note (signed by Redwood Ops) for exports delivered via managed transfer.
- Scheduling: request via compliance@redwood.com with preferred delivery channel and target window. For Greenline specifically, we can commit to a 48–72 hour turnaround for the initial SOC 2 fieldwork export if you confirm scope by EOD tomorrow.

-Marissa

Sara —

Thanks for the questions. Please find consolidated answers below. I've attached a small sample manifest (admin_activity_manifest_sample.csv), a one-page Export Playbook (export_playbook.pdf) with delivery options, and a standalone checksum file (checksums.sha256).

Quick answers (audit-ready bullets):
1) Events captured: sign-in/login (console & API), auth failures, user/service-account lifecycle (create/disable/delete), roles/permission changes, API key/secret lifecycle, consent/OAuth client changes, and explicit admin policy edits. Each event record includes timestamp (UTC), actor id/email, actor IP, user-agent where present, a request-id/correlation-id, target resource id, and an action type. Sensitive values are redacted.
2) Retention: default 180 days. Extended retention (1/3/7 years) is available for Dedicated/Private customers or via paid retention blocks for Hosted. On-demand snapshot exports covering arbitrary windows are supported.
3) Export formats and delivery: CSV, JSONL, gzipped tar shards. Bundles include a CSV manifest (filename, start/end UTC, record counts, SHA256 per file). Delivery: SFTP push, presigned S3/GCS/Azure links, or secure Drive ACL. Both full and incremental (delta) exports supported.
4) Integrity: SHA256 for every file; manifest-level SHA256. Redwood-managed HMAC-SHA256 signing is standard. PGP/GPG signing with customer keys is available for Private deployments or as part of an enterprise agreement.
5) SLA: standard one-off export — 3 business days; expedited (24–48h) for an additional fee. Exports can include soft-deleted records when requested; permanently purged data beyond retention cannot be recovered.

Attachments: admin_activity_manifest_sample.csv (manifest layout), export_playbook.pdf (delivery options & checklist), checksums.sha256 (example).

If you confirm the scope (time window + preferred delivery channel + whether you need soft-deleted records), we will schedule the export and provide a signed chain-of-custody manifest. Marissa noted we can do 48–72h turnaround for Greenline if you confirm scope by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks and let me know if you need this in CAIQ/SIG-friendly wording — we can translate to the questionnaire artifacts.

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
